brief.headline: Close the 16.6% price gap on PET bottles — ₹28644 annual saving is on the table from a supplier earning peer-level margins with an A-stable rating.

priceAsk.summary: Match Suraj Blow Plast's ₹1.87/NOS on the PET BOT AMBER 100ML/25MM NECK 12.5G bottle
priceAsk.basis: We pay Suraj Blow Plast ₹1.87/NOS for the identical SKU — a 16.6% gap. Closing it recovers ₹28644 annually. TPAC's 3.8% net margin matches the peer median of 3.7%, so there is no margin squeeze preventing parity.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 Days After Receipt to 45 Days (peer median is 33d payable, so 45d is achievable)
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: An additional 15 days releases ₹46539 in working capital for FDC

brief.financialLeverage: TPAC is financially stable — [ICRA] A / Stable rating, 0.19x debt-to-equity, 4.55x interest coverage, and a 62/100 health score. Net margin of 3.8% sits at the peer median of 3.7%, and EBITDA margin of 10.4% is healthy. However, they squeeze suppliers hard: 17d payables versus peer median 33d, yet stretch receivables to 67d (peer 65d). Our ₹11.32 L is only 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue, so we have near-zero individual leverage. But their strong balance sheet and investment-grade rating mean we can push firmly on price and terms without continuity risk — and we have four credible alternates if they resist.

evidence.point: We overpay by 16.6% on the key PET bottle SKU versus our best-in-house price
evidence.figure: Gap: 16.6%, our price ₹2.18/NOS, best price ₹1.87/NOS from Suraj Blow Plast

evidence.point: TPAC's net margin matches the peer median, so no underlying cost disadvantage
They pay suppliers in 17 days, half the peer median of 33 days — they extract aggressive terms upstream
Investment-grade credit rating confirms financial strength
Our spend is immaterial to them
Estimated annual excess cost on rigid plastic packaging totals ₹28644

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter covering pharma bottles, caps, and preforms — top second-source candidate already flagged in our system

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-packaging leader with A-grade health, serving pharma; robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle and jar specialist (Pearlpet brand) — direct fit for our PET bottle requirement

risks: We are only 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue — minimal single-account leverage; must bundle volume, extend commitment, or credibly pivot to Manjushree or Mold-Tek to gain traction
GST filing delays and EPF payment delays are on record — may signal administrative stress or cash tightness despite the A-stable rating; monitor continuity if we push hard
Their 17d payables show they demand tight terms from their own suppliers; they may resist giving us better than 30 days unless we offer volume or multi-year lock-in
Return on capital of 7.6% lags the peer median of 13.4% — profitability per rupee invested is weak, which may make them defensive on price even though absolute margin is in line
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to understand why we're paying ₹2.18 per bottle when our best price for the identical PET item is ₹1.87 — that's a 16.6% gap we need to close this year.
